nonvacuity: scratch/FiniteChecks.lean compiles checks that the five-point baseline is normalized, every atom has strictly positive mass, and both endpoint response discrepancies are genuine. T1 is a closed conjunction with no hypotheses; no vacuous implication is involved. The exact rho=1/5 contrasts are also independently checked there and in scratch/exact_checks.py.

scratch/FiniteChecks.lean compiles an existential instance rho=1/5 satisfying 0<=rho<=1 and rho>0, and independently computes both advertised contrasts. The baseline is a normalized law with all five masses positive. Thus all outer hypotheses, including the strict-positivity subcase, are jointly satisfiable.

scratch/FiniteChecks.lean: checkStanding16 independently proves all four assumptions for finiteSampleWitness, including whole-triple treatment independence and every nondegeneracy clause. occupiedSample=[0,8,0,8] is proved to lie in D with strictly positive iid four-sample mass. scratch/exact_checks.py independently enumerates the nine observable atoms and all 9^4 ordered observable samples, reproducing the singleton covariances, P(D), all six moments, both variances, and their nonzero difference.

scratch/MeasureChecks.lean compiles an example satisfying every hypothesis of T4WholeStatement: E=Fin 8 with its discrete measurable space, nu=(1/8)*count, and W,X,Y,Z,V from distributionWitness. It proves IsProbabilityMeasure nu, measurability of all five coordinates, the almost-sure bound V<=2, and all four standing assumptions. Its bridgeMean lemma establishes the actual Bochner integral equals the finite weighted sum. No audited theorem T1-T5 is used in these proofs.

scratch/FiniteChecks.lean: checkStanding8 independently proves every standing assumption for distributionWitness. A compiled example gives both affirmative conditioning cells probability 1/4 and computes the t=0 discrepancy as control probability 1/2 versus treated-plus-one probability 0. scratch/exact_checks.py also checks the conditional support values. All functions are measurable and bounded on the finite population.
